records.name: American Friends Service Committee
records.summary: A Quaker peace and service organization with its main office in Philadelphia. It works on peace and justice issues and runs projects across the country and abroad. Its website does not list programs that are only for Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Join a listed public event, take part in the weekly Friday Action Hour, sign up for updates, or look at the volunteer and careers pages.

schedule.text: Action Hour every Friday at 12 p.m. Eastern time, online. Other events are listed on the events page.

cost.text: Joining the online events is free. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Sign up for AFSC news and actions on the website, then register for a public event listed on the events page.
first_step.basis: The events page lists events with sign-up links, but it does not say which are in Philadelphia, whether they are online, or what a first event is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The website does not describe a first visit to the Cherry Street office, and it lists no open house or Philadelphia volunteer shift. The weekly Friday Action Hour starts at noon Eastern time, and the events list links each event to its own page or a sign-up page. Ask the office at 215-241-7000 what an event involves and whether it costs anything before you register.
first_visit_tips: The Action Hour starts at noon Eastern time, which is 9 a.m. Pacific.
Ask whether an event is online or in person before you sign up.
The office does not list walk-in hours, so call before you come to 1501 Cherry Street.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the Friday Action Hour is online. The event pages read on this visit did not state the format, so the word online is carried over unconfirmed. The Oct 29 event on the events page (a values-based financial planning session) has no year written, so last_sign_of_life is carried from tier 1 and could not be re-checked on this visit. The current Action Hour is titled for Palestine on its event page. Event costs are not stated on the events page. No Philadelphia-only events or volunteer shifts were found.

records.name: Andrée Collective
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that uses weddings and celebrations to offer jobs and counseling referrals to women who survived intimate partner violence or human trafficking. Supporters can give monthly or attend its annual gala.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to the Celebrations for Freedom Gala, join the monthly Party 29 giving program, or apply through the group's Opportunities page for its board, its Emerging Leaders Council (ages 18 to 35), or an unpaid part time marketing internship.

schedule.text: One big event each year, a gala with a silent auction. Other events are listed on the upcoming events page.

cost.text: Gala tickets start at $125 for early-bird pricing. Party 29 is an optional monthly gift of $29 or $124.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to the 2026 gala through the group's ticket page, or use the I'm Interested button on the Opportunities page to ask about a board or council seat.
first_step.basis: Anyone can buy a gala ticket, and board and council roles have a clear interest button. The pages do not describe what a first board meeting or council event is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The 2026 gala is a gala and silent auction at The Arts Ballroom, 1324 Locust Street, with thanks to its sponsors. The page gives no start time, no program details, and no list of who attends, and it shows photos from the 2025 event. Board members meet about six times a year, including a retreat, and are asked to make a personal gift.
first_visit_tips: Early-bird gala pricing ends October 8, so buy before prices rise.
The gala page has no accessibility details, so contact the group about wheelchair access, quiet space, or ASL before you go.
The board and council use the same I'm Interested button, and no deadline is listed.

records.notes: The gala venue (The Arts Ballroom, 1324 Locust St., 19107) is in what_to_expect rather than locations, because it is one event's venue. Party 29 gifts are $29 (one group therapy session) or $124 (a month of sessions). The board meets six times a year. The internship is unpaid, part time, hybrid, about 4 to 8 hours a week, and applied for by email to a named staff member (address on the page, not recorded here). No deadlines are listed on the opportunities page. The 2025 gala date (Nov 2, 2025) comes from tier 1 and is carried into last_sign_of_life.

records.name: Annunciation B.V.M. Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 10th and Dickinson streets with Masses in English and Spanish, a Hispanic ministry and an adult faith formation program. It also runs religious education for children and hosts parish events such as a St. Nicholas Italian Festival.
records.what_you_do: Join a Mass in English or Spanish, sign children up for religious education, take part in adult faith formation such as the Lent movie series or a Bible study, or start the adult initiation program (OCIA) for people who want to join the Catholic Church. The site also links the FORMED online faith library.

schedule.text: Saturday Mass at 5 pm in English. Sunday Masses at 9 am (Spanish) and 11 am (English). Weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 7:30 am in the chapel, with Spanish Mass on Monday and Thursday at 7 pm. Spanish-speaking groups meet on several weeknights, and English classes for Spanish speakers meet Tuesday and Thursday at 12:30 pm.

locations.label: Parish church
locations.address: S.E. corner of 10th and Dickinson Sts. (rectory at 1511 S. 10th St.)

first_step.how: Come to a Saturday or Sunday Mass, then email the parish office at annunciation19147@gmail.com or call 215-334-0159 to ask about a program.
first_step.basis: The adult initiation page says people exploring the Catholic faith can start at any time, and it gives an email and phone number to ask. Masses are open and free, but the site does not say how a newcomer starts most other programs.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and you can come in without signing up. The Saturday Mass is in English, the Sunday 9 am Mass is in Spanish, and the 11 am Mass is in English. Adults who want to join the Catholic Church can start the OCIA program at any time; its sessions meet Wednesday evenings at 7 pm for about an hour, from September to the Easter Vigil.
first_visit_tips: Confession is heard Saturdays 4 to 4:45 pm and Thursdays 6 to 6:45 pm, and at other times by appointment through the rectory.
The parish is on the southeast corner of 10th and Dickinson streets, and the rectory is at 1511 S. 10th Street.
The site does not list ramps, elevators, or parking, so call 215-334-0159 before you come if you need access help.

records.notes: The religious education (CCD) fee and registration are not recorded. The program page names a 2024 to 2025 year and lists a registration contact at a different parish (St. Anthony of Padua), so it looks out of date; confirm with the parish. The OCIA page gives no start date. The Hispanic ministry contact (Veronica Cinto, annunciationchurch958@gmail.com) is on the Spanish side of the site and is not recorded here. The Cada Semana page lists weekday and date pairs with no year, and the pairs do not line up with 2026, so they are not used as dated evidence. Its Wednesday 7 pm English class meets at Saint Anthony of Padua school (9th and Pierce), a different site, so it is not in the schedule text. No accessibility details on the pages read. Daily-readings dates on the home page are not evidence of activity.

records.name: Arcadia Commons
records.summary: Neighbors who look after three green spaces in East Kensington so people have places to gather: Kern Park, The Huntingdon Emerald and the Emerald Wildflower Garden.
records.what_you_do: Sign up to water Kern Park or help tend its garden beds, join the mailing list, or give a donation. The group also runs free BBQs and workshops at its green spaces.

schedule.text: Volunteer shifts, such as watering Kern Park, are posted on sign-up sheets. The website lists no fixed weekly work days or times.

locations.label: Kern Park
locations.address: Kern Street, between E. Huntingdon and E. Sergeant Streets

locations.label: The Huntingdon Emerald and Emerald Wildflower Garden

cost.text: The website lists no fee for volunteering or joining, and it accepts donations.

first_step.how: Sign up for a watering shift at Kern Park through the group's sign-up link, or email info@arcadiacommons.us to ask about other volunteering.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page invites neighbors to take part and posts a sign-up link. It does not describe what a volunteer shift is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Watering Kern Park is the only task the volunteer page names. The site does not say how long a shift runs, what to bring, or whether children can help, so ask before you go. No fee is listed for volunteering.
first_visit_tips: Kern Park is on Kern Street between East Huntingdon and East Sergeant streets.
Ask the group what to bring, since the site lists no gear or age rules.
Confirm the shift time and place by phone or email, because the sign-up page did not show a readable sheet on this visit.

records.notes: Status changed from probably_active to dormant because the newest dated item on the news page is a post dated June 24, 2024, which is older than 24 months. The volunteer and sign-up pages carry no dates, so current activity is unconfirmed. The sign-up link opened a generic SignUpGenius page, not the Kern Park sheet. Before this shows as active, confirm with the group (phone or email) whether watering and other volunteer work is still running. Kern Park history dates (1912, 1913) are not evidence. Older 2017 news items mention Nature Heroes workshops and a Gardens for Good vote; they are not recorded as leads because no website was found.

records.name: Arch Street Friends Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting in Old City where people sit together in silent worship on Sunday mornings and on Wednesday evenings on Zoom. Families can use a children's program during the school year.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship in person, the Wednesday evening worship on Zoom, or the adult education series on fourth Sundays. Greeters welcome newcomers on Sundays, and refreshments follow worship. Ask the office how to get involved in committee and outreach work.

schedule.text: Sunday worship from 10:30 to 11:30 am at the meetinghouse. Wednesday worship from 5:30 to 6:30 pm on Zoom. A children's meeting runs on the first to third Sundays from September to June, 10:30 to 11:15 am.

cost.text: No dues or fees are stated. The children's program and childcare are free.

access.notes: The entrance and restroom are wheelchair accessible, and a hearing loop is available. The children's room is on the second floor, and the pages read do not mention an elevator.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am, where a greeter will meet you. Children from Pre-K through 8th grade can join the Children's Meeting on the first to third Sundays.
first_step.basis: The site has a Newcomer Resources page, greeters meet visitors on Sundays, and visitors are invited to attend. It has no orientation or first-timers event on the pages read.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship lasts an hour, from 10:30 to 11:30 am, and it is held in silence with no leader or planned program, though someone may speak. A greeter meets you, the hour ends with a handshake, and a social time with refreshments follows. On the first to third Sundays, children can join the free Children's Meeting, and younger children can use free childcare during worship.
first_visit_tips: Free, limited parking is on site during worship. The lot entrance is on 4th Street, halfway down the block from Arch Street.
Check septa.org for current transit routes, since the pages do not name a stop.
The website suggests watching an introductory video about Quakerism before a first visit.
The Wednesday Zoom link is in the weekly bulletin and the calendar, not on the pages read.

records.notes: Tier 1 said Sunday worship was also held on Zoom. The worship page does not mention Zoom at all, so Sunday Zoom is left out of the schedule text; the Wednesday Zoom session is on the home page. Pages give dates with no year (for example an October 11 children's meeting and worship, and an October 12 memorial meeting), so no dated evidence was recorded and status stays probably_active. Children's Meeting ages (Pre-K to 8th grade) come from its own page. Adult education runs on fourth Sundays September to June, with no sign-up described. Wheelchair rating is partial because the children's room is upstairs and no elevator is mentioned.

records.name: Arch Street Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A downtown Presbyterian congregation on Arch Street with Sunday worship, a music ministry, small groups and outreach to partner missions.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship at 10:45 am, which has a Zoom option, or join the choir, a small group such as the Wednesday Zoom Good Book Club, or a family program.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:45 am. The Good Book Club meets every Wednesday from 12:10 to 1 pm on Zoom. The choir rehearses before and after worship each week and sings at least three Sundays a month.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:45 am, then email info@archstreetpres.org to ask about a small group, the choir, or family programs.
first_step.basis: Worship is public with a Zoom option, and the choir and the Zoom Bible group say everyone is welcome and give a way in. The site has no page that spells out a visitor welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The pages do not describe a Sunday service, but children are welcome in the 10:45 am worship and a nursery is available. The Good Book Club is a Zoom session every Wednesday from 12:10 to 1 pm, and the choir welcomes anyone who wants to learn, with no audition mentioned. The pages read give no cost for worship, groups, or the choir.
first_visit_tips: Free street parking on the west side of 18th Street, between Arch and Cherry, is for Sundays from 9 am to 6 pm only, and you need a placard from the sanctuary or the website.
The home page links a childcare registration form, so register ahead if you need the nursery.
The office is open Monday to Thursday, 8 am to 4 pm, at 215-563-3763. The pages do not cover accessibility, so ask there.
The directions page recommends SEPTA, including Suburban Station and the City Hall stops, with a short walk to the church.

records.notes: Status is active because the small groups page carries a Wednesday, December 17, 2025 session date with its year written. That page also lists the PEACE Book Club, a one time listing with no recurring schedule, so it is left out of schedule text. The Good Book Club Zoom link is on the church website but was not on the pages read. Children's church time and nursery hours are not stated. The music ministry page describes one choir only. The choir director's contact is on the music page; it is not recorded here, and the church office can route questions.

records.name: Arlen Specter US Squash Center
records.summary: A squash center that runs junior programs, a summer squash camp for players of every skill level, lessons, and club events.
records.what_you_do: Kids and teens can join junior programs, lessons, and the summer squash camp, and adults can take lessons too. You can book a court online. The site also lists memberships and venue rentals, and it does not list volunteer coach or mentor roles.

schedule.text: Open every day. Weekday hours close at 8 or 9 pm (the site lists both), and weekends run 9 am to 5 pm. Junior programs and lessons are scheduled on the online calendar.

locations.label: Center on the Drexel campus, University City

cost.text: Prices for lessons, junior programs, and memberships are not published on the pages read. Summer camp is paid in full at sign-up to reserve a spot.

first_step.how: Browse the online calendar, choose a junior program, lesson, or adult class, and register online. Contact the team for help, especially if it is your first time.
first_step.basis: The site says all levels are welcome, the summer camp takes beginners, and it invites first-timers to contact the team for help.
first_step.what_to_expect: Players are grouped by age and skill, from beginners up to competitive juniors. Summer camp runs 9 am to 3 pm for full days or 9 am to noon for half days, with lunch provided and optional care until 5 pm. Prices are not listed on the pages read, so ask before you book.
first_visit_tips: Plan on non-marking sneakers and eyewear; the center lists both among the items you can borrow or buy.
Summer camp drop-off can start at 8:30 am.
30th Street Station is about two blocks away, according to the visit page.
Metered street parking is nearby, and the visit page lists garages at 3440 Market Street and 3386 Chestnut Street.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: 30th Street Station (regional rail), about two blocks away, as named on the center's visit page.

records.notes: No street address is recorded. The center's own site does not publish one, and two public sources disagree: Wikipedia lists 3205 Lancaster Avenue, and the SquashSmarts West Philadelphia page (a program run from the center) gives 25 N. 33rd Street. Confirm before adding an address. The site gives two sets of weekday hours (close at 8 pm in one place, 9 pm in another), so the schedule text says so. Camp dates carry no year on the page, which also refers to 2025 to 2026 camps. Camp needs at least 4 paying players each week to run. US Squash, the national body whose mailing address is on the contact page, is not listed as a lead. The tennis_pickleball tag is the nearest racquet sport because no squash tag exists. Email addresses on the contact page are hidden and are not recorded.

leads_only.name: Alcoholics Anonymous meeting at 1924 S. 7th Street
leads_only.note: Named on the parish's Spanish page with meeting information. The meeting itself was not checked, and no own website was found.

blocked.note: Not a bot block, but the Kern Park sign-up link returned a generic SignUpGenius page, not the sheet. No dates or open slots could be read.

notes: Seven groups, all publish. Verdict counts: publish 7. Searches used 1 (a search for the Specter Center street address; see its record notes). Fetches used 34, with no rate limiting seen. Status changes from tier 1: Arcadia Commons moved from probably_active to dormant (newest dated item June 24, 2024). Status for Arch Street Presbyterian moved to active on a December 2025 date written with its year. Corrections to tier 1: Arch Street Friends' Sunday Zoom claim is not confirmed by the worship page; Annunciation's CCD page looks out of date and its fee was not recorded; the AFSC Action Hour 'online' claim is carried over but could not be confirmed. Dated events were removed from schedule text. Not made into leads: Saint Anthony of Padua (named only as the site of an English class), US Squash (named as a mailing address), and Nature Heroes (named in 2017 news, no website found). The Cherry Street office for AFSC has no walk-in hours on its site.
